6-1 momentum: prior return from 126 to 21 days ago, skipping the last month to strip out short-term reversal while keeping the underreaction-driven trend.
10-day return scaled by its own volatility: a trend achieved with low risk reflects steady information-driven demand rather than noisy swings, so it persists more reliably than raw return.
Monthly vs half-year EMA crossover: identifies trend acceleration relative to a slower institutional-timescale reference.
Elevation above the half-year low: a larger confirmed recovery from a salient trough signals durable improving sentiment that persists.
Recency of the half-year high: the longer since the high was set, the more likely the trend has already stalled, so freshness predicts persistence.
Staleness of the half-year low: a durable gap in time since the last trough marks a well-established, self-reinforcing recovery.
Half-year information discreteness: sustained day-by-day consistency over two quarters is a stronger continuation signal than an equal return from sporadic jumps.
9-month information discreteness: the longest-window consistency measure, capturing whether a slow trend has been a steady grind that keeps underreacted-to.

Open-price gap relative to the close 2 sessions earlier captures multi-session drift into the open; dislocations from a stale reference price tend to partially correct as the session's liquidity is supplied.
10-day price-participation correlation: a rising price with rising dollar volume confirms genuine demand and predicts continuation, versus a rise on fading volume.
Monthly price-volume trend correlation: healthy uptrends are accompanied by growing participation, a pattern more durable than a price rise on thinning interest.
3-day reversal filtered by accrual quality: firms with earnings running ahead of cash flow are more prone to sentiment-driven overreaction and mean-revert more reliably than low-accrual names.
Half-year momentum interacted with profitability: momentum in high-ROE firms is more likely driven by genuinely improving fundamentals and less likely a crowded, fragile trade.
Monthly range expansion vs a half-year baseline, signed by trend: a slower-forming volatility breakout in a clear direction reflects a more durable regime change.
Break of a 2-month average price confirmed by a volume surge relative to a 90-day base: broader participation behind a break is more durable than a break on quiet trading.
Break of a quarterly average price confirmed by rising monthly volume relative to a half-year base: volume-confirmed breaks of longer averages mark more durable regime shifts.
9-month-high proximity discounted by leverage: anchoring-driven continuation near a high is more durable for low-leverage firms than for highly levered ones facing distress risk.
Proximity to the half-year high confirmed by elevated relative volume: the anchoring effect is strongest when fresh highs are made on above-average participation, not thin conviction.
Quarterly momentum weighted toward lower-dollar-volume names: even within the S&P 500, relatively less-liquid names are slower to fully impound information, so their momentum persists longer.
5-day price-volume correlation, inverted: when a short-term price rise is not confirmed by a rising volume trend, the move is more likely a temporary squeeze than durable demand, and it reverses.

A standardized 6-day average share-volume level proxies short-lived investor attention; freshly crowded, high-volume names keep absorbing momentum flow that pushes prices further, so the level itself carries near-term return information.
Same liquidity-uncertainty mechanism as the 21-day version measured over 35 days, capturing a slightly more persistent regime of unstable trading interest that commands a risk premium.
The gap between a stock's share-count-volume rank and its dollar-value rank isolates low-priced-stock volume concentration, a retail/lottery-demand signature that predicts subsequent reversal.

Ranking today's traded value against only its own trailing 5 days isolates idiosyncratic liquidity surges from market-wide ones; an idiosyncratic surge is dominated by short-lived liquidity trading that mean-reverts.

A stock's own 21-day volume percentile captures whether today's participation is elevated relative to its recent regime; elevated self-relative volume signals unresolved information flow still being absorbed, predicting continuation over the window's horizon.
Same re-emergence-from-a-dry-spell mechanism as the 90-day version but measured against a 150-day regime, capturing longer liquidity droughts before renewed participation begins.

The direction of the 63-day change in volume, weighted by the stock's own 63-day volume percentile, flags names undergoing a decisive, self-relative participation regime shift rather than routine noise, which precedes continued price adjustment.

A positive 3-day correlation between volume and price means the recent trend has been confirmed by participation rather than drifting on thin liquidity; volume-confirmed trends are more likely information-driven and continue.

Volume co-moving with the size of daily returns over 5 days is the classic signature of new information hitting the tape; stocks currently showing this linkage are mid-way through an information event, predicting continued volatility-adjusted drift.
Same information-event signature as the 5-day version, measured over 8 days to confirm the volume-volatility linkage is not a single-day artifact.
Amihud-style price impact: how much a stock moves per dollar traded measures immediate illiquidity; investors demand higher expected returns to hold names with high per-dollar price impact.

Today's range relative to its own 5-day norm flags a sudden liquidity/volatility shock; range expansions of this kind are associated with information events whose price impact keeps unwinding over the next few sessions.

Unusually costly price discovery (wide range per dollar traded) happening in a name with contemporaneously high share volume is a distress signature - even active trading isn't enough to keep the market orderly - a state that commands a same-day liquidity-risk premium.
A sudden burst of attention on a name with questionable earnings quality is when informed short-sellers are most likely acting on the accrual signal, so the interaction targets that specific moment.
An efficient asset base combined with a same-day volume shock flags operationally sound firms suddenly drawing fresh scrutiny, the moment a stale efficiency story is most likely to be repriced.

Same idiosyncratic-attention-regime mechanism applied to the earnings-per-share level over 30 days, flagging names where a durable earnings characteristic is coinciding with fresh, self-relative liquidity interest.
Same idiosyncratic-attention-regime mechanism applied to asset turnover over 18 days, flagging operationally efficient names catching fresh, self-relative liquidity interest.

A same-day inverted liquidity rank scaled by profitability flags genuinely high-quality names momentarily out of favor with liquidity providers, a mispricing most exploitable exactly when attention is thinnest.

Profitable firms that are also durably high-attention (elevated smoothed volume z-score) are the ones institutional flows keep bidding toward fair value, so their combination should carry positive, slow-decaying return information.
Same informed-trading-ahead-of-recognition mechanism as the accrual-gap version, applied to a change in leverage confirmed by an above-baseline volume surge.
Same informed-trading-ahead-of-recognition mechanism applied to a change in ROA confirmed by an above-baseline volume surge, flagging a profitability shift being acted on early.

Dividing accrual gap by the 63-day relative volatility of volume isolates names whose earnings-quality signal is not yet reflected in erratic trading, i.e. stable-liquidity names where the accrual anomaly is least likely to be noise-driven.
Same regime-shift-direction mechanism as the leverage version, applied to accrual gap over 21 days to flag whether an earnings-quality concern is being newly discovered or abandoned.
Same regime-shift-direction mechanism applied to asset turnover over 30 days, flagging whether an efficiency story is being newly discovered or abandoned by participation.

Same regime-shift-direction mechanism applied to the earnings-per-share level using a dollar-volume delta over 18 days, flagging whether an earnings story is being newly discovered or abandoned by capital flow.

A 3-day volume-return correlation confirms whether recent price action in a profitable name is backed by real order flow; profitability determines whether that flow-confirmed move is a re-rating worth extrapolating.

Interacting leverage with a 12-day Amihud illiquidity measure isolates highly levered names specifically among stocks that are costly to trade, where solvency-related mispricing is least likely to have been arbitraged away.
Same actively-voting-with-volume mechanism as the leverage version, applied to accrual gap to flag questionable-earnings names undergoing conviction-backed repricing.
Same actively-voting-with-volume mechanism applied to ROE, flagging profitable names undergoing conviction-backed repricing.
Same same-day-liquidity-shock mechanism applied to operating margin, flagging high-margin names undergoing an acute, same-day price-impact event.

Weighting accrual gap by today's price-impact-per-share ties earnings-quality risk to an instantaneous market-depth shock, flagging names where thin same-day depth coincides with questionable accounting.
Weighting accrual gap by the time since the widest single-day range in the last 21 days flags questionable-earnings names still being re-tested around a past acute liquidity event.

Scaling ROE by leverage isolates operating profitability from financial amplification; investors who extrapolate headline ROE without this adjustment overvalue leverage-driven returns and underprice equally profitable but safer firms.

A composite of high profitability, high margin, and low leverage proxies the quality-minus-junk construct; investor preference for lottery-like risky growth names causes systematic underpricing of boring, safe, profitable firms.

Generating more revenue per dollar of assets reflects a leaner, more scalable operating model whose efficiency is not a headline reported ratio, so the market is slow to connect current turnover strength to future margin gains.

A firm sitting near the top of its own short-term profitability range signals a locally strengthening earnings regime that extrapolative analysts diagnose with a lag, so self-referenced strength predicts further upward revisions.

This margin information-ratio rewards high average profitability relative to its own dispersion, and investors overweight generic volatility as risk while underpricing the quality premium that attaches to genuinely predictable margins.

Stable, not just high, asset turnover indicates a repeatable operating process rather than lumpy asset sales, and this lower operating-risk profile is underpriced relative to noisier peers with similar average turnover.

This measures efficiency generated per unit of balance-sheet leverage, and firms that turn assets over quickly without relying on debt carry lower financial risk for a given operating profile, a safety premium the market does not fully price versus more levered peers.

This scales smoothed margin by the magnitude of smoothed accrual aggressiveness, since margins backed by low accruals are cash-based and higher quality than equally-high margins propped up by aggressive accrual choices that the market pays for without adjusting.

Ranking firms inversely by smoothed margin volatility captures that erratic margins raise the discount rate investors apply for earnings unpredictability, so structurally stable-margin firms deserve a valuation premium the market under-applies in real time.

A long exponential average of the accrual gap isolates the firm's structural reliance on accrual-based earnings from single-quarter noise, better identifying chronic earnings-management behavior than any one report.

Rewarding smoothed asset profitability only for firms with below-peer-average leverage isolates earnings quality that is not manufactured with financial leverage, so the safer subset is under-priced relative to its true risk-adjusted quality until the market recognizes the distinction.

Rewarding the smoothed price-free earnings yield only for firms with below-average accrual levels combines cheap-on-book with cash-backed earnings, the combination least likely to be reversed by future write-downs, a joint condition the market underprices relative to its persistence.

Over a multi-quarter horizon, firms with genuinely improving profitability should be rewarded for margin strength reflecting durable pricing power, while firms whose profitability has been trending down for roughly two quarters are better characterized by their financial risk, so rotating the rewarded dimension follows the trajectory the market is slow to update on.

Efficiency gains that coincide with a positive very-recent return show technical and fundamental signals already agreeing, and agreement between two independent channels lowers the odds either is noise, favoring continuation.

When turnover is improving and return and volume are tightly co-moving (directional flow, not choppy noise trading), the price action looks informed, reinforcing that the efficiency gain is already being traded on with conviction.

Standardizing both the fundamental surprise and the trading-activity surprise cross-sectionally puts them on comparable scales, so their product isolates a genuinely unusual joint move rather than being dominated by whichever series has fatter tails that day.

When margin is higher than it was three weeks ago recent momentum is left to run, since momentum in improving-quality names tends to be genuine; when margin is deteriorating the same recent return is inverted, because a rally into worsening fundamentals looks more like a technical bounce that mean-reverts.

Margin expanding over the past couple of months while the stock still sits near the bottom of its own trailing price range signals that price hasn't caught up to the improved profitability yet, a lagged-recognition setup that should close as the market re-rates the name.

A tight link between volume spikes and range expansion indicates a disorderly, liquidity-driven price-discovery regime; highly levered firms are more exposed to forced-selling cascades in such regimes, raising crash risk.

Rising volatility-of-volatility signals an unstable risk regime where refinancing terms and covenant risk are most sensitive; highly levered firms suffer disproportionately when the volatility regime itself turns erratic, a tail-risk premium level volatility alone misses.

Expensive valuation and high leverage jointly make equity value acutely sensitive to discount-rate shocks; when realized volatility rises, this combination flags elevated risk of a sharp valuation de-rating.

A sustained decline in return on equity signals deteriorating shareholder value creation; when trading volume has stayed persistently low, the deterioration has likely not yet been actively traded, implying a delayed re-rating once attention returns.

Smoothing the return-volume correlation before ranking yields a stable measure of whether price moves are persistently volume-confirmed, identifying firms where low earnings quality is consistently accompanied by distribution-like trading.
Smoothed short-term earnings yield, ranked cross-sectionally, filters single-day price noise to reveal a genuine cheap-valuation tier that attracts value buying as the discount is recognized.
Combining the long-run direction of book-yield change with a short-run volume percentile flags stocks structurally cheapening amid unusually high participation, consistent with informed accumulation.

A fresh 21-day low (small TS_ARGMIN) in an otherwise profitable firm often reflects indiscriminate, liquidity-driven selling rather than a change in fundamentals; subtracting recency-of-low from a profitability rank targets that short-term overreaction for a mean-reversion bounce.

The sign of a recent change in dollar volume shows whether trading interest in a name is expanding or fading; multiplying earnings rank by that sign favors profitable firms currently drawing more interest, where information is more likely to be actively priced in.

Covariance between price changes and dollar trading activity approximates informed order flow moving the price; ranking it alongside profitability isolates efficient firms whose recent moves are backed by real transaction flow rather than thin, easily reversed trades.

Stable, historically consistent trading activity tends to accompany efficient, well-understood pricing; subtracting a quarter-long trading-value-variability rank from a margin rank favors high-margin firms whose liquidity has not been erratic and can re-rate without noise-trading interference.

Recency of a name's own 21-day volume peak signals that new information is being actively traded on right now; multiplying by a profitability rank targets fundamentally sound firms experiencing that fresh burst of interest, when informed trading is most likely to be moving price toward fair value.
